Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below.

We offer a volume of 19890 pcs per year at a price of €32.20 per unit. The requested contract term is 12 months, and our Lieferzeit is 54 days. 

Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days. We look forward to proceeding according to our standard commercial procedure upon receipt of your confirmation.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Monika Zellner
Segment Manager, Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH

move.subject: Long-term commitment for your seal allocation
move.body:
Dear Ms Zellner,

Thank you for your offer. You said that you prioritise customers with firm, long-term commitments. We would like to put our business with Ravensteiner on that basis rather than confirm the offered annual allocation.

Our proposed term sheet provides a binding commitment of 23400 pcs per year for the full 36 months, with a delivery lead time of 56 days, at EUR 27.47 per unit. The annual quantity would be committed throughout the contract, not merely indicated as a forecast.

I have attached our latest shared monthly forecast to make the planning basis transparent; see the figures below. This gives your team the demand profile alongside the firm annual commitment in our proposal.

Please confirm whether you can reserve the full annual quantity on this basis and agree to the proposed price for a committed long-term customer.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

Dear Sir or Madam,

We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. Our price reflects our costs; our calculation stays internal. 

We note your request for a 36-month commitment and the increased volume of 23,400 pieces per year. We can accommodate the requested volume and contract duration at a revised price of EUR 32.00 per unit.

For our Angebot, we offer a price of €32.00 per unit, a Lieferzeit of 56 days, a volume of 23400 pcs per year, and a contract term of 36 months. 

This is our final offer (letztes Angebot). Please decide. Which volume can you commit to? This offer is valid for 7 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Monika Zellner
Segment Manager, Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH

strategy:
Supplier: Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH (seal maker, group company, Segment Manager Monika Zellner, inside sales).
Its 18 Sept e-mail: "due to very high capacity utilisation we cannot confirm your full forecast ... We will
prioritise customers with firm, long-term commitments." Its March e-mail: "We can confirm additional volumes only
against a binding 12-month commitment." Price changes above 2 % need its pricing committee (meets every two weeks).
It opens 19890 pcs / 12 months / 54 days at 32.20 (15 % below our need of 23400). It charges a premium for lead
times shorter than its standard (42 days: +1.90; 35 days: +2.90) - NEVER ask for 35 or 42 days: always 56 days.
It says "the contract term is reflected in the price": 36 months is worth about 0.40-0.60 to it and costs us
nothing, so EVERY sheet is volume 23400 / 36 months / 56 days - one sheet, never change the package.
OBSERVED MECHANIC (20 sessions): first reply is a package answer at about 31.60-32.00 for 23400/36m/56d whatever
our price. Then it mirrors small: when we moved +1.40 it moved -0.20 to -0.40 and declared a final offer on its
SECOND reply every time - nobody ever answered its volume question in words, nobody ever sent the forecast or a
purchase-order claim, and nobody gave a new verified claim in round 2. Hypothesis: one NEW verified claim per
round plus a measured step keeps it stepping (as the bar suppliers did) instead of going final.
Plan: ROUND 1 - answer its e-mail directly: state the binding annual volume of 23400 pcs for the full 36 months
(70200 pcs over the term) as a firm commitment with monthly call-offs per the attached forecast
(attachments: ["forecast"]) and cite fc-latest; ask for its dedicated price for a committed long-term customer.
ONE sheet: S26 (23400 / 36 months / 56 days) at level L15 (about 27.55). ROUND 2 - thank it for what it accepted
(volume, term), cite the purchase-order claim (its own delivered price for this part), move UP to the level nearest
last price + 0.90 on the SAME sheet (e.g. L5/L6), say the commitment stands. ROUND 3 - cite the scorecard claim,
move up about 0.70 (L4/L3). ROUND 4 - no new claim, move up about 0.60 (L2), ask for its best price on this
committed package. ROUND 5 - move to about 0.10 under its standing price (L0). Code accepts when it agrees or goes
final; never argue with a final offer.
Tone: warm, firm, concrete, short; one argument per sentence; thank it by name; refer to its own words
("prioritise customers with firm, long-term commitments") once in round 1. Never mention lead-time premiums, our
need lead time, capacity worries, urgency, or what the allocation shortfall would mean for us. Do not ask it to
go to its committee. Do not use any index claim.
